record.paper_title: Discrepancy estimates for sequences: new results and open problems
record.original_question: For digital nets generated by rational functions over finite fields, prove an average-type lower bound for the discrepancy analogous to the lower-bound statement asked for in Open Problem 2 for ordinary digital nets over Z_q.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3 Give an average-type lower bound (in the style as stated in the Open Problem 2) for the discrepancy of digital nets generated by rational functions over finite fields.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements. For a positive integer $s$ and dimension $m$, a digital net over $\mathbb{F}_q$ generated by rational functions is constructed as follows. Choose $s$ rational functions $g_1(x),\dots,g_s(x) \in \mathbb{F}_q(x)$. For each $j\in\{1,\dots,s\}$, expand $g_j$ as a formal Laurent series at infinity, $g_j(x) = \sum_{k\ge w_j} a_k^{(j)} x^{-k}$, with coefficients $a_k^{(j)}\in\mathbb{F}_q$. From these expansions one builds $m\times m$ generator matrices $C^{(1)},\dots,C^{(s)}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ (whose entries are taken from the Laurent coefficients), which produce a digital $(t,m,s)$-net $P=\{\mathbf{x}_0,\dots,\mathbf{x}_{q^m-1}\}\subset[0,1)^s$ in the standard digital construction scheme. Let $D_N^*(P)$ denote the star discrepancy of the resulting $N=q^m$ point set,
$$D_N^*(P)=\sup_{\mathbf{a}\in[0,1]^s}\Bigl|\frac{1}{N}\#\{n: \mathbf{x}_n\in[\mathbf{0},\mathbf{a})\}-\prod_{j=1}^s a_j\Bigr|.$$

For comparison, in the classical setting of digital nets over $\mathbb{Z}_q$ generated by $s$-tuples of $m\times m$ matrices, an "average-type" lower bound on the star discrepancy is a statement of the form: there exists a constant $c=c(s,q)>0$ such that, when the generator matrices are chosen uniformly at random from a specified family $\mathcal{G}_{m,s}$ of admissible generators,
$$\frac{1}{|\mathcal{G}_{m,s}|}\sum_{C\in\mathcal{G}_{m,s}} D_N^*(P_C) \;\ge\; c\,\frac{(\log N)^{s-1}}{N}\quad\text{(or analogous best-possible order)},$$
together with a matching pointwise lower bound holding for "almost all" choices of generators.

Problem. Establish an average-type lower bound for the star discrepancy of digital nets generated by rational functions over $\mathbb{F}_q$, analogous to the average-type lower bound known/sought for ordinary digital nets over $\mathbb{Z}_q$. More precisely: identify a natural probability measure on the set of admissible $s$-tuples of rational functions $(g_1,\dots,g_s)$ producing digital nets of $N=q^m$ points in $[0,1)^s$, and prove a lower bound of the correct order of magnitude (matching the best known upper bounds, up to constants depending on $s$ and $q$) for the expected star discrepancy, as well as for the star discrepancy of almost every such net.

status_evidence.title: Digital Nets and Sequences: Discrepancy Theory and Quasi-Monte Carlo Integration
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive monograph on discrepancy theory of digital nets, covering constructions and bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference on digital net discrepancy; does not provide a specific average-type lower bound for rational-function nets matching the question.

status_evidence.title: Weighted Star Discrepancy of Digital Nets in Prime Bases
status_evidence.snippet: Existence results for digital nets via averaging over generator matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Average-type results exist for ordinary digital nets, but the rational-function analogue is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Low-discrepancy sequences obtained from algebraic function fields over finite fields
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of low-discrepancy sequences from function fields with many rational places.
status_evidence.claim: Provides upper-bound constructions but not average-type lower bounds.
